correctness.rationale: Direct two-state CTMC conditioning yields the exact mean, covariance, and mixed third moment formulas. Positive covariance weights make the exponential decomposition unique. Equal rates are recovered by a quadratic; distinct rates by a complete four-sign analysis, whose only nontrivial collision is complementary occupancies with unequal rates. In that class, one third-order lag has a nonzero sign-reversing factor, proving identification. A twofold exact rational witness and 90 two-time-kernel algebra tests corroborate the argument. This is population moment, not finite statistical identification.

originality.rationale: The exact blind-spot locus for all stationary two-site heterogeneous immigration/extinction rates is a statement about the full second-order temporal moment hierarchy and a single higher-order moment, not an observed-law equivalence theorem. Royle-Kery use identifiable site-labelled occupancy and detection models, Bernstein-Sheldon use one common individual transition matrix, and general aggregated-Markov canonical results describe observational laws, not this sharp second-moment exception. Query comparisons disclosed below reveal no specific stronger-covered statement. The unrestricted general literature is an important unresolved risk, not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Ecologists tracking counts of occupied habitats rather than individual identities must distinguish patch-specific local extinction and colonization. The theorem gives a complete structural criterion for when even every second-order temporal statistic loses that heterogeneity information, and one minimally richer moment restoring it at any positive lag. The ambiguity is genuinely realized by positive-rate pairs. This is an exact observability boundary, not a routine single-parameter substitution or a parameter-grid recomputation; the model assumptions and sensitivity near equality limit practice.
